question: The anterior pituitary gland:

options.opa: It is part of the hypothalamus.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Anterior pituitary gland" -> "regulated by hormones from hypothalamus" -> "hormonal regulation" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Anterior pituitary gland" -> "secretes hormones into bloodstream" -> "hormonal communication" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Anterior pituitary gland" -> "not part of hypothalamus" -> "separate structure" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Anterior pituitary gland" -> "does not release ADH and oxytocin" -> "ADH and oxytocin released by posterior pituitary" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Anterior pituitary gland" -> "formed by endocrine cells" -> "not formed by neurons" -> 90%
analysis: The anterior pituitary gland, also known as the adenohypophysis, is regulated hormonally by releasing hormones from the hypothalamus. It does not release ADH and oxytocin; these hormones are released by the posterior pituitary gland (neurohypophysis). The anterior pituitary is not part of the hypothalamus, nor is it formed by neurons; it is composed of glandular tissue. Therefore, the correct option is that it is regulated hormonally.
